flip.SI-20211103-046970-L: FLIP THRESHOLD: **the seating rule, not a field.** If the seat were released at the release (an 'event-aware seat' rule — hold the cell's position until the scheduled event, then re-seat), this candidate would not spend SI/NY at 13:02 and the FOMC's own candidates would be reachable. No term of my policy is close to flipping (T4 43/95 = 45%, T1 14/30, T3 163s), so the only number that matters on this row is a PROTOCOL number: 06:57:10 to the event, printed on the sheet, in a phase that closes 09:57:09 after it.

novel.SI-20211103-046970-L: novel (day 11): **THE EVENT-BLINDNESS OF EARLIEST-ROW SEATING, quantified on the block's biggest event day.** S12's `next_scheduled` countdown is strictly ex ante and printed on every row; the NY phase (13:00-22:59) contains the FOMC statement; my two seats are spent 6h57m and 5h29m before it, and the 128 creation-class candidates of the day — the largest count in the block — are forfeited by the seating rule rather than by any judgement. **This is a stage-1/stage-2 architecture finding, not a reader error: a one-position-per-phase policy on a 10-hour phase must decide WHETHER TO SPEND THE SEAT EARLY OR WAIT FOR A KNOWN EVENT, and nothing in the program's decomposition (seat existence -> side -> moment) currently expresses that choice.** I am recording it, not trading it: an event-aware seating rule is a change to the replay contract (CC-M2-10.3), not to my policy.
